header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec> --run`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/shir_native_command_v_sync.txt
not a copy of it.  The `cv_path`/`cv_absent` rows measure the model's hypothesis
(every name the fold's list carries really resolves on this machine) with bash,
so the status law is not resting on an unchecked assumption.

pins.stmt_expr: IrStmt::Expr(IrExpr::Call { func: "exec".to_string(), args: vec![st("command"), IrExpr::Array(vec![st("-v"), st("ls")])] })
pins.note: `command -v ls` is a known name: the fold fires and writes status true -- bash exits 0

pins.stmt_expr: IrStmt::Expr(IrExpr::Call { func: "exec".to_string(), args: vec![st("command"), IrExpr::Array(vec![st("-v"), st("nonexistent")])] })
pins.note: the literal `nonexistent` is the one name the fold calls absent: status false, bash exits 1
residue check, executed: both source copies repeat the same name list; this compares them name by name for every name in it
a name outside the list is unknown to the pass, so the condition keeps the shell-out

pins.stmt_expr: IrStmt::Expr(IrExpr::Call { func: "redirect".to_string(), args: { let mut a = cv_redirected(cv_spec(1, "w", "/tmp/cv_out")); a[0] = IrExpr::Arrow(vec![cv_call("-v", "ls")]); a } })
pins.note: `command -v ls > /tmp/cv_out` would put the path in the file, so the statement fold refuses
the condition fold only fires behind `> /dev/null`; any other sink keeps the shell-out
a flag other than -v is a different question (`command -V ls` prints a description), so it keeps the shell-out
d1: the statement fold also fires on the bare form, where bash prints the resolved path and the fold prints nothing
the fold's list is an unconditional claim: every name in it folds to status 0
d2, measured: the list names programs the machine may lack (python here); the fold says 0 where bash exits 1
the model's other hypothesis: `nonexistent` really does not resolve
